text: The Apollo seismometers were switched off in 1977, and nobody has listened to the inside of the Moon from its surface since. This small station is meant to start again, in a region no instrument has ever visited.

text: Plants have grown on the space station for years, in weightlessness. Nobody yet knows how they behave in one sixth of Earth's gravity, under the radiation of the open lunar surface.

objectives.text: Land a crew on the Moon

lines.text: Launch attempt 1 stopped at T−18 minutes: a hydrogen leak at the fuelling arm. Next attempt in 6 days.
Lift-off from Kennedy Space Center on 23 Apr 2033, 88 days before the deadline.
The boosters burned out and fell away on time.
The escape tower was dropped, unused.
Core Stage burned out and fell away. The stack is in space.
Parking orbit. The crew and mission control check every system before leaving Earth.
The third stage restarted and burned for about six minutes. Speed needed: 12.37 km/s. The rocket delivered it.
1 course correction on the way out, 2 m/s in total.
Three quiet days. The Earth shrinks in the window.
Braking burn behind the Moon, out of contact with Earth. 30 minutes of silence, then a voice: the burn was good.
The spacecraft settled into a high, slow orbit and docked with the lander that was sent ahead.
Touchdown, 0.3 km from the planned point. Engine off.
6 moonwalks, about 48 hours outside in all.
Science on the surface: 127 of 114 planned points so far.
Lift-off from the Moon. The crew is together again in orbit.
The engine fired behind the Moon one last time. The spacecraft is on its way home.
The capsule met the air at 11 km/s.
Three parachutes. Splashdown 6 km from the planned point.
The crew is aboard the recovery ship within the hour after splashdown.

flight.headline: The crew reached the Moon but did not land

objectives.text: Land a crew on the Moon

lines.text: Launch attempt 1 stopped at T−18 minutes: a hydrogen leak at the fuelling arm. Next attempt in 6 days.
Lift-off from Kennedy Space Center on 23 Apr 2033, 88 days before the deadline.
You dropped the boosters 0.8 s early. Unburned propellant fell away with it: −7 m/s.
You dropped the core stage 1.0 s late. An empty stage rode along as dead weight: −8 m/s.
The stack is in space.
Parking orbit. The crew and mission control check every system before leaving Earth.
The third stage restarted and burned for about six minutes. Speed needed: 12.37 km/s. The rocket delivered it.
1 course correction on the way out, 2 m/s in total.
Three quiet days. The Earth shrinks in the window.
Braking burn behind the Moon, out of contact with Earth. 30 minutes of silence, then a voice: the burn was good.
The spacecraft settled into a high, slow orbit and docked with the lander that was sent ahead.
The commander took the controls for the last hundred metres.
The descent went outside safe limits. The computer called the abort and fired the ascent engine.
The crew is back in orbit.
The engine fired behind the Moon one last time. The spacecraft is on its way home.
The capsule met the air at 11 km/s.
Three parachutes. Splashdown 6 km from the planned point.
The crew is aboard the recovery ship within the hour after splashdown.

causes.effect: Weather at Kennedy Space Center stopped one launch attempt. Waiting for clear skies cost 1 day.
2 launch attempts were stopped by technical faults. They cost 8 days and 0.3% of the budget.

causes.decision: Stage 6  ·  First stage: kerosene booster, four engines
causes.effect: Thrust-to-weight at lift-off was 0.93. Below 1, a rocket cannot leave the ground.

flight.headline: The rocket never left the pad

objectives.text: Land a crew on the Moon

lines.text: Launch attempt 1 stopped at T−31 minutes: a valve that did not close. Next attempt in 4 days.
Launch attempt 2 stopped at T−21 minutes: high winds above the pad. Next attempt in 4 days.
Launch attempt 3 called off at T−37 minutes: lightning within reach of the pad. Next attempt in 1 day.
Ignition. The engines reached full thrust and the rocket did not move: it weighs more than its engines can lift. The computer shut them down.
